first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent it, so I read it properly on the iPad. It's sensible and calm, not gushing, and I liked that it promises 'No grading tables, no prices, no rules.' The ring is really her and her fiance's business, though, so I'm reading it to understand what she's on about, not to make a decision.

journey.quote: No grading tables, no prices, no rules. Just proportion, preference and light.
journey.reaction: Good. Nobody's trying to sell me a diamond. That makes me trust the rest more.

journey.quote: GIA separates the two: shape is the outline of the diamond seen from above, while cut style is how the facets are arranged and angled, which changes the sparkle and the overall look.
journey.reaction: Quoting the gemological institute rather than their own opinion is reassuring. I didn't know the difference myself, and now I do.

journey.quote: It has a high crown, a small table and a compact hall of mirrors effect, and many show an "X" pattern face-up.
journey.reaction: Crown? Table? Pavilion further down? They're never explained. I had to guess. A line saying what these parts of the stone are would help someone like me.

journey.quote: Those sharp corners need a protective setting to prevent chipping.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of practical point I'd want my daughter to hear before anyone pays. I'll mention it to her.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: When you are ready to plan, Wedded Concierge looks after venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One named person from start to finish is exactly what I want. But 'payments' is where my ears prick up: whose account, what currency, and is the deposit protected? It doesn't say, and it doesn't say what the service itself costs.

unanswered_questions: What does the Wedded Concierge service cost, and are fees agreed in writing?
When the concierge handles 'payments', are quotes in AUD and are deposits protected if an overseas supplier folds?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked?
Who do we ring if something goes wrong overseas outside business hours?
would_share_with: My husband, mainly the concierge paragraph, with the question of what it costs

cta_reaction.quote: You can talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: 'Talk to' sounds like a phone call, which I'd like, but this is a ring article and nothing here tells me about fees, deposits or contracts. I'd click only once my daughter says they're seriously looking at overseas, and only to find out who's accountable for the money.

top_3_changes: In the concierge paragraph, add one plain line on how fees and payments work (fees agreed in writing, AUD quotes), next to 'looks after venue, travel, vendors and payments'.
Explain 'table', 'crown' and 'pavilion' in a few words the first time they come up.
Make it clear the 'talk to a Wedded Concierge' link leads to a real conversation, ideally a phone call, with no obligation.

Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, sent the link by her daughter)
No invented brand facts; missing information listed under unanswered_questions
